coverage: Covering roughly Nov 24–25, 2026. Compiled Wednesday, ET.

items.headline: The AI selloff spreads to Asia, and Nvidia slips before the open
items.summary: Japan took the hardest hit overnight: per @MilkRoadAI, SoftBank fell as much as 16% to a 52-week low, with Kioxia, Advantest and Tokyo Electron each down about 12-14%, while the broader Topix lost only about 1%. Their read: a targeted unwind of the AI winners, not a market-wide panic. Korea's KOSPI tripped a sell-side sidecar a day after a 6% rally. @KobeissiLetter then reported Nvidia down more than 5% in premarket trading. Jim Cramer's one-line diagnosis: "Anthropic is the silent killer of this market."
items.short: A targeted unwind of AI winners, not a broad panic.

items.headline: Google's Neon model wins over the builders
items.summary: Google said Neon set a Day-1 usage record on its paid APIs and that Antigravity tokens per day are up 82% in the six weeks since Argon launched; Elon Musk quoted it with "Impressive work by Google." Practitioners agreed: @sriramk called Neon his go-to on a variety of tasks, "perhaps the first GDM model to do so," and @simonsarris said he won't do more GPU or translation work without it, though he still keeps organized with Opus because of its better VS Code tooling.

items.headline: Palmer Luckey: the 'take the cash' crowd doesn't get Jensen
items.summary: A day after Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, Scott Galloway suggested on Kara Swisher's show that Huang would be happier admitting a mistake, helping pick a new CEO and walking away with $180 billion. Palmer Luckey's reply was the most-liked post in the feed overnight: "Zero theory of mind or any understanding whatsoever of what motivates people."

items.headline: BNP Paribas downgrades Micron, sees memory parity a year sooner
items.summary: Per @MilkRoadAI, BNP Paribas cut Micron to Neutral and halved its price target, arguing DRAM and NAND supply and demand could near parity by mid-2027 rather than mid-2028, with less HBM in Nvidia's Vera Rubin Ultra. The counterpoint: Korean media report Samsung's memory capacity is mostly contracted through 2029.

items.headline: Serenity: SanDisk's long-term contracts carry 80% margin floors
items.summary: @aleabitoreddit noted SanDisk has long-term agreements with contractual price floors that management says deliver at least 80% gross margin every year, plus customer deposits for 2029-2031 capacity per Morgan Stanley, and argued NAND prices don't need to keep rising for memory names to look cheap.

items.author: RoboStrategy
items.text:
Inside the humanoid company Google is training its robot brain on.

@Apptronik co-founder and CEO Jeff Cardenas (@jeffcardn) sat down with @herbertong and @GoingBallistic5 to talk about what Apollo has to prove as GXO plans to deploy up to 1,000 of them over the next four years.

Apollo is already running kitting pilots on Mercedes-Benz lines in Hungary and Germany, performing at 96% efficiency against a human benchmark. Jeff says Apollo 3 will be shown next year, on wheels or legs, and Apptronik plans to build thousands of them after hundreds of Apollo 2s.

Jeff on Google's Gemini:
"While Gemini can work great on other robots, it performs best on Apollo because it was trained on Apollo."

Jeff on home robots:
"My timeline for home robots and highly capable robots has been pulled in by years in the last several months."

items.title: GPU prepayments change what matters
items.author: Gavin Baker
items.summary: As GPU clusters shift from offtake agreements to customer prepayments, Baker argues operating cash flow to EBITDA becomes the key metric, and diligence moves from private-credit funds to the customers paying nearly 100% upfront. Dock-to-live time and cluster stability become what buyers judge, and GPU payback periods shorten.

items.title: A dot-com survivor on this crash
items.author: A.J. Manaseer
items.summary: Manaseer traded a college account up to $500K in the dot-com era and lost it all. He contrasts the junk of 2000 with today's AI suppliers, sold out for years and hugely profitable, and argues this selloff is the opposite kind of crash. Worth reading as a memoir of how leverage and hype feel from inside.

items.title: Four Cards
items.rule: If a card has a vowel on one side, it has an even number on the other.
items.explanation: E could hide something that breaks the rule; 3 breaks it if the other side turns out to be E. 4 can't break it (the rule never says only those cards have it), and T isn't covered by the rule at all. Most people pick the card that matches the rule's second half instead of the one that could falsify it.
